parsed.explanation: The combined federal–state regime is high risk. Federal M/F passport/visa rules create traveller-facing entry friction: mismatch can trigger case-note refusal, additional evidence, and permanent-ineligibility risk if wilful misrepresentation is found. Federal government-funded single-sex facility exclusion, misgendered custody, and severe immigration/corrections abuse are tier-1 exposures; counterterrorism wording and allied advisories add threat framing. The state/province is assessed low-risk for adults, with governor vetoes, municipal non-discrimination, and employment protections, moderating local facility and street risk. It does not pre-empt federal border, facilities, or detention. Minors/travelling families face youth-care, sports, school-reporting, and national care-policing rules, raising exposure above adult-only risk. No execution is documented, so not extreme-severe; severe custody and minor rules keep it below protective jurisdictions.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal M/F-only passports/visas; mismatch triggers case-note refusals, additional evidence, permanent-ineligibility risk if wilful misrepresentation is found. Reports include blocked/confiscated passports, stranded travellers, and allied advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; legal challenges continue; waivers possible only with limited criteria; legal-aid traveller FAQ documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal gate applies regardless of state/province protective layer; document discrepancy can move traveller into investigation or removal/detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections adopts conversion-therapy-like inmate policies, removes hormones; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; misgendered placement documented; counterterrorism frames pro-transgender ideology as hostile.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several federal orders blocked/enjoined; courts hear challenges; no documented effective protection for a visitor facing federal detention.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border/facility disputes or visa status can feed into immigration custody; state low-risk does not pre-empt federal detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal bar on congruent facility access in government-funded single-sex spaces; other states have criminal bans and documented arrest/trespass charge with men's-ward placement; state/province map shows many bans.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State/province assessed low-risk for adults, governor vetoed bathroom/pronoun bills, no mapped ban, and nine cities have ordinances.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local protections reduce state facility risk, but federal facilities and funding rules remain operative; private settings uncertain.

care_services.exposure: Minor care restricted: surgery ban, Medicaid exclusion, sports ban, school reporting; national proposals cut youth insurance coverage; custody removes HRT.
care_services.protection: State executive order covers state employees over 21 and bars conversion-therapy funding; county conversion therapy ban; no documented blanket adult traveller HRT ban.
care_services.interaction: Adult care may be denied through federal facility/custody encounters; family/minor care seeking can trigger institutional scrutiny or exclusion.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal binary-sex order, trans-page removal, DOJ reward memo mentioning radical gender ideology, and 2026 strategy naming radically pro-transgender groups; allied travel advisories.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal Title VII, national hate-crime coverage, state executive and municipal non-discrimination, and governor vetoes.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal hostility can escalate immigration or federal-facility contacts even where local police are restrained; state layer does not erase national framing.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor can be denied sports/surgery, face school-reporting or investigation, and encounter care refusal; parents/guardians can become questioned, investigated, or separated from care.
minors_guardians.protection: State governor vetoed bathroom/pronoun bills; family-court intervention limited to imminent harm; one county conversion-therapy ban.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor status activates youth-targeting laws beyond adult exposure; national orders and state rules combine during schooling/care/sports encounters.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-directed local violence or arrest documented for this state/province; bias law omits gender identity and panic defence remains.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and Title VII cover gender identity; municipal ordinances and state employment order apply.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local restraint may reduce street policing, but federal custody/facility encounters remain hostile; absence of local incidents is not safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Litigation and injunctions are partial; SCOTUS allowed passport restrictions; enforcement varies by administration, city, private setting and crossing; no reliable protection from federal facility/immigration exposure.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, ongoing civil-liberties suit, state/municipal complaint paths, and some enjoined orders exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Travellers cannot know whether a dispute resolves through courts, consular contact, or federal detention; minor protections especially unsettled.

anchor_checks.comparison: Above 0.15: no documented routine months-long pretrial custody for presentation or capital provision; state/province adult layer is protective. Similar severe custody and immigration abuse, but less immediate criminalization.

Around 0.25: shares birth-sex custody and facility criminal exposure, but local state/province has no adult ban and protective ordinances; federal immigration sexual abuse and minor rules balance upward/downward.

Below 0.45: worse than routine checkpoint humiliation/administrative denial because federal government-funded facilities, custody abuse, immigration sexual abuse and counterterrorism threat framing are operative.
Much below 0.75: protective care/health charter absent at federal layer; 0.75 has no credible severe custody exposure. Here federal border, facilities, and detention create high consequences.

parsed.synthesis: Federal hostility dominates for any outed traveller: M/F document checks can lead to refusal, permanent bar, federal facility exclusion, and severe immigration/corrections custody. The state/province's low-risk adult profile and municipal protections reduce local bathroom/street risk but cannot pre-empt federal border, federally funded facilities, or detention. Adult alone sits in high-risk band due conditional severe custody rather than routine execution; travelling with a trans minor is more dangerous because youth care, school reporting, sports bans, and national criminalising teachers create family exposure even without local adult targeting. Enforcement is contested, so practical risk depends on timing and which authorities encounter the traveller.
